translations.text: And the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will have no end.
Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen to me, since I have not had sexual relations with a man?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one you give birth to will be called the Son of God.
And look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For no word from God will fail.”
Mary said, “Here I am, the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel left her.
At that time Mary got up and went with haste into the hill country, to a town in Judah.
She entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby leaped for joy in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She cried out in a loud voice and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.
Why has this been granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come?
For as soon as the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby leaped for joy in my womb.
And blessed is she who believed, for what the Lord told her will be fulfilled.”
And Mary said, “My soul magnifies the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
because he has looked upon the lowly condition of his servant. For from now on all generations will call me blessed.
Mary stayed with her for about three months and returned [?] to her own home.
A decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole inhabited world should be registered.
This registration took place when Quirinius was governing Syria.
And everyone went to be registered, each to his own town.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he belonged to the house and family of David.
He went to be registered with Mary, his betrothed wife, who was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
And she gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in swaddling cloths, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.
And there were shepherds in the same region, staying awake and keeping watch over their flock at night.
And behold, an angel of the Lord stood among them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were very afraid.
And the angel said to them, “Do not be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy that will be for all the people.
For Christ the Lord has been born to you in the city of David.
And this will be the sign for you: you will find a baby wrapped in cloths, lying in a manger.”
And suddenly there was a voice to the angels [?], a multitude of heavenly warriors.
“Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, goodwill among people.”

And when the angels had departed from them into heaven, the men, the shepherds, said to one another, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
And they hurried there and found Mary and Joseph, and the baby lying in a manger.
When they saw him, they told what had been said to them about this child.
And all who heard were amazed at what the shepherds told them.
But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart.
And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
And when eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
And when the days of purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought the child up to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male child who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,”
and to offer a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord: “Two turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
And there was a man in Jerusalem whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was in him.
And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
And he came into the temple led by the Spirit. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what was customary under the law,
he took him into his arms, and Simeon blessed God and said,
“Now, Master, you are letting your servant depart in peace, according to your word,
for my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the sight of all peoples,
a light for revelation to the nations, and the glory of your people Israel.”
And his father and mother were amazed at what was being said about him.
And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and as a sign that will be opposed.
And a sword will pierce your own soul too, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
And there was a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very advanced in years, having lived with her husband for seven years after her virginity.
And she was a widow until the age of fourteen. She did not leave the temple, serving with fasting and prayer day and night.
And coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to the Lord and spoke about him to all who were waiting for redemption in Jerusalem.

And when everything had been completed according to the Lord’s law, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth. And the child grew and became strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was upon him.
And the child grew and became strong, being filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was upon him.
And his parents went to Jerusalem every year for the feast of Passover.
And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast.
And when the days were over, as they were returning, the child Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, and his parents did not know it.
Thinking that he was in the traveling party, they traveled for five days and looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
And when they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem, searching for him.
And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
All who heard him were astonished at his understanding and his answers.
And when they saw him, they were amazed. His mother said to him, “Child, why have you treated us this way? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in distress.”
And he said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be occupied with the things of my Father?”
And they did not understand what he said to them.
And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.
And Jesus grew in wisdom and in stature, and in favor with God and people.

In the twelfth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pilate governed Judea, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch of Iturea and the region of Trachonitis [?], and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
And he went throughout the whole region of the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
As the word is written in the books by Isaiah the prophet, who says, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked ways will become straight, and the rough paths smooth.
And all flesh will see the salvation of God.
He said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, “You offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
So produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
For the axe already lies at the root of the tree [?]. Every tree, therefore, that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”
And the crowds asked him, saying, “Teacher, what should we do?” [?]
He answered them, “Whoever has two tunics should give one to someone who has none, and whoever has food should do the same.”
Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Collect nothing beyond what you have been instructed to collect.”
Soldiers also asked him, saying, “And what should we do?” He said to them, “Do not mistreat anyone or accuse anyone falsely, and be worthy of your promises [?].”
As the people were waiting expectantly and wondering in their hearts about John, whether he was the Christ,
John answered, saying, “I baptize you with water, but someone stronger than I is coming. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into his granary, but he will burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.”
And telling many other things, he spoke to the people.
At that time Jesus entered Nazareth, where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to him. He unrolled the scroll and found the place where it was written:
“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. He has sent me to bring good news to the poor and to heal the brokenhearted,
to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to set the oppressed free, to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
He rolled up the scroll, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on him.
He began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
And everyone listened to him and marveled at the gracious words coming from his mouth.
“Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his own homeland.
But I tell you in truth, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the heavens were shut for three years and six months, and there was a famine throughout the land.
Yet Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, but none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”
And he filled [?]
of the Son. So will the coming of the Son be. [?] paralyzed. And they were trying to bring him in and lay him before him.
And finding no way to bring him in because of the crowd, they climbed onto the roof and lowered him through the tiles, with his bed, in front of Jesus.
And when Jesus saw their faith, he said to him, “Man, your sins are forgiven.”
And the scribes and Pharisees began to reason, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
But Jesus, knowing their thoughts, answered them, “What are you thinking in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man—“I tell you, get up, take your bed, and go home.”
And immediately he stood up before them, picked up what he had been lying on, and went home, glorifying God.
And they were filled with fear, saying, “We have seen wonderful things today.”

Jesus stood on a level place, with a crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon, who had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases.
And those who were suffering from unclean spirits were healed.
And the whole crowd was trying to touch him, for power was going out from him and healing them all.
And he lifted his eyes toward his disciples and said:
“Blessed are you who are poor in spirit, for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
Blessed will you be when people hate you, when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and leap for joy, for your reward in heaven is great.”
The Lord said, “As you want people to treat you, treat them in the same way.
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the same.
And if you lend to those from whom you expect to receive repayment, what credit is that to you? For even sinners lend to sinners to receive the same amount back.
But love your enemies, do good, and lend. [?] fell among thorns, and the thorns grew and choked it.
At that time, Jesus entered Capernaum.
A certain centurion had a servant who was sick and dying, and whom he valued highly.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent Jewish elders to him, asking him to come and save his servant.
And when they came to Jesus, they pleaded with him earnestly, saying, “He is worthy of whatever you grant him.
For he loves our nation and built us a synagogue.
Jesus went with them. When he was not far away, the centurion sent friends to him, saying to him, “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.
That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes.”
When Jesus heard this, he marveled at him, and turning to the crowd following him, he said, “Truly I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith.”
When those who had been sent returned to the house, they found that the sick servant had been healed.
When neither of them had anything to repay him with, he forgave them both. Which of them will love him more?
Simon answered, “I suppose the one whom he forgave more.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
Turning toward the woman, he said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? You gave me no water for my feet, but she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed my feet with fragrant ointment.
For this reason I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, because she loved much.”
He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Those reclining at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who even forgives sins?”
He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
[?] fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it.
Other seed fell on good soil, sprouted, and produced a crop a hundred times as much.
His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

He said to them, “It is for you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but for the others they are given in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not hear or understand.
This is what the parable means: the seed is the word of God.
Those along the path are the ones who hear the word of God. Then the devil comes and takes the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are the ones who receive the word with joy when they hear it. But they have no root: they believe for a time, and in a time of testing they fall away.
What fell among thorns represents those who have heard but are overwhelmed by worries, riches, and the pleasures of life, and do not bring their fruit to maturity.
What fell on good soil represents those who hear the word with a good and upright heart, keep it, and bear fruit with perseverance.
The Lord told this parable: “No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing is concealed that will not become known and come to light.
So pay attention to how you listen. For whoever has will be given more, but whoever does not have will have even what they think they have taken away.
His mother and brothers came to him, but they could not speak to him because of the crowd.
He was told, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
But he answered them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”
At that time, as Jesus was coming into the region of the Gadarenes,
a man from the city met him. He had been possessed by a demon for many years. He wore no clothes and did not live in a house, but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he fell down before him and said in a loud voice, “What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

For Jesus was commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. It had seized him for many years, and people bound him with iron chains and shackles and kept watch over him. But he would break his bonds and be driven by the demon through the wilderness.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
They begged Jesus not to order them to go into the abyss.
Now a large herd of pigs was grazing there on the hillside. The demons begged him to let them enter the herd of pigs, and he allowed them to enter.
The demons came out and entered the herd of pigs. The whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned in the water.
When the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the villages.

Crowds came out of the city to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at Jesus’ feet, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
All the people of the region of the Gergesenes begged him to leave them, because they were overcome with great fear. Jesus got into the boat and returned.
The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to be with him. But Jesus sent him away, saying,
“Return to your home and tell how much God has done for you.” And he went throughout the whole city, proclaiming how much Jesus had done for him.
At that time, a man named Jairus came to Jesus. He was a leader of the synagogue. Falling at Jesus’ feet, he begged him to come into his house,
because his only daughter, about twelve years old, was ill and dying. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed against him.
And there was a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years. She had spent all she owned on physicians, but could not be healed by any of them.
She came up from behind and touched the hem of his garment, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When everyone denied it, Peter and those who were with him said, “Master, the crowds are jostling you and pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
But Jesus said, “Someone touched me, for I felt power go out from me.”
When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she fell down trembling. Falling before him, she told all the people why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
Jesus said to her, “Go; your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader and said to him, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher.”
When Jesus heard this, he answered him, saying, “Only believe, and she will be saved.”
When he came to the ruler’s house, he allowed no one to enter with him except Peter, John, James, and the father and mother.
Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But Jesus said, “Do not weep. The girl is not dead, but asleep.”
The people laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But he put them all outside, took her by the hand, and called out, saying, “Girl, get up!”
Immediately her soul returned, and she rose at once. He ordered that she be given something to eat.
Her parents were astonished. But Jesus instructed them strictly, saying, “Tell no one what has happened.”
At that time, Jesus called his twelve disciples and gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.
He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: neither a staff, nor a bag, nor bread, nor silver, nor two tunics, nor copper money.”
“Whatever house you enter, stay there, and leave from there.”
“Wherever they do not welcome you, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that town, as a testimony against them.”
They set out and went through the villages, proclaiming the good news everywhere.
At that time, as Jesus came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
A man from the crowd cried out, saying, “Teacher, I beg you, look at my son, for he is my only child.”
“A spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out and goes into convulsions, foaming at the mouth. It scarcely leaves him, battering him.”
“I begged your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered him, saying, “You unbelieving and corrupt generation! How long will I be with you and put up with you? Bring your son to me.”

While he was still speaking, the demon threw the boy down, shaking him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, saying, “Unclean spirit, come out of the boy!” He was healed at that very hour, and Jesus gave him back to his father.
The people marveled at the majesty of God.
At that time, as Jesus was traveling along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.”
Jesus said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead, but you go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Another also said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first let me say goodbye to those in my house.”
Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
“Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever listens to me listens to the one who sent me. Whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
The seventy returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name.”
He said to them, “I saw Satan fall from heaven like lightning.”
“Look, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.”
“Nevertheless, do not rejoice that the spirits submit to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.”

At that moment Jesus rejoiced in spirit and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent and revealed them all to little children. Yes, Father, for this was pleasing to you.”
At that time, an expert in the law came to Jesus to test him, saying, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, with all your strength, and with all your mind, and love your neighbor as yourself.”
Jesus said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered him, “A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers. They stripped him, wounded him, and went away, leaving him barely alive.”
“By chance a priest was going along that road, and when he saw him, he passed by.”
“Likewise, a Levite came to that place, saw him, and passed by.”
“But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came to him, and when he saw him, he had compassion on him.”
“He approached him and bandaged his wounds, pouring oil and wine on them. Then he put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and cared for him.”
“The next day, as he left, he took out two denarii, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, ‘Take care of him, and whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.’”
“Which of these three, then, do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell among the robbers?”
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
At that time, Jesus entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him into her house.
She had a sister named Mary, who sat at Jesus’ feet and listened to his word.
Martha was occupied with much serving. She came up and said, “Lord, do you not care that my sister has left me alone to serve you? Tell her, then, to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.
But one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good portion, which will not be taken away from her.”
Yours [?]. Your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
Give us our daily bread each day.
And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves forgive everyone who owes us. And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.
The Lord said to his disciples, “Which of you has a friend and goes to him at midnight and says to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves,
for a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’?
And he will answer from inside, ‘Do not trouble me. The doors are already shut. I cannot get up and give you anything.’
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless persistence he will get up and give him as much as he needs.
And I tell you: ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks the door will be opened.
Which father among you, if his own son asks for bread, will give him a stone? Or if he asks for a fish, will he give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
If you, then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give the good Spirit to those who ask him!”
While he was saying this, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that you sucked!”
But he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it!”
The Lord told this parable: “A certain rich man’s field yielded abundantly.
And he thought to himself, saying, ‘What shall I do? I have nowhere to gather my crops.’
And he said, ‘This is what I will do: I will tear down my barn and build a larger one, and there I will gather all my grain and my goods.
And I will say to my soul, “You have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.”’
But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your soul will be taken from you. And whose will the things you have prepared be?’
So it is with anyone who stores up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God.” Having said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!”
The Lord said, “Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been pleased to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give to the poor. Make yourselves moneybags that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in heaven, where no thief comes near, no worm gnaws, and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will also be.
Keep your belts fastened and your lamps burning.
And be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open the door for him immediately.
Blessed are those servants whom the master finds doing this when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will fasten his belt, seat them at the table, and come and serve them.
Whether he comes in the second watch or in the third watch and finds them awake, blessed are those servants.
But know this: if the master of the house had known, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
You too must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.
At that time, Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And there was a woman who had had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her to him and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your illness.”
He laid his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and glorified God.

But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, said, “There are five days on which work ought to be done. Come on those days and be healed, and not on the Sabbath day.”
Jesus answered him, “Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to give it water?
And should not this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound for these eighteen years, have been freed from her bonds on the Sabbath day?”
As he said this, all who opposed him were put to shame, and all the people rejoiced in him because of all the glorious things he was doing.
The Lord told this parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man takes and plants in his garden. It grew and became a large tree, and the birds of the sky nested in its branches.”
And again he said, “To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like yeast that a woman took and hid in flour until all of it had risen.”
Jesus passed through towns and villages, teaching and making his way toward Jerusalem.
Someone said to him, “Lord, are only a few being saved?” And he said to them,
“Strive to enter through the narrow gate, for many, I tell you [?], will seek to enter and will not be able to.

Once the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, ‘Lord, Lord, open it for us.’ And the master will answer you, ‘I do not know where you come from.’
Then you will begin to say, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught in our streets.’
And he will say to you, ‘I do not know where you come from. Depart from me, all you who do evil.’
There will be weeping and grinding of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves cast out.
And many will come from the east and the west, and from the north and the south, and recline at table in the kingdom of God.
At that time, Jesus went into the house of one of the leaders of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat bread.
And they were watching him closely. And there before him was a man suffering from dropsy.
And Jesus responded by saying to the experts in the Law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath?” But they remained silent.
And he took hold of him, healed him, and sent him away.
And he said to them in response, “If any of you has a donkey or an ox that falls into a well, will he not immediately pull it out on the Sabbath day?”
And they could give him no answer to this.
And he told a parable to those who had been invited, observing how they chose the places of honor. He said to them:
“When you are invited to a wedding feast, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more honored than you is among those invited.
Then the one who invited both you and him will come and say to you, ‘Give this man your place,’ and then, in shame, you will begin to take the lowest place.

But when you are invited, go and sit in the lowest place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will have honor among all those invited with
you. For everyone who exalts himself is humbled, and whoever humbles himself is exalted.”
The Lord told this parable: “A certain man prepared a great supper and invited many.
And at the time for supper he sent his servants to say to those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’
And they all began alike to make excuses. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it. Please excuse me.’
And another said to him, ‘I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’
And another said, ‘I have married a wife, and for this reason I cannot come.’

And that servant returned and reported this to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly to the crossroads and streets of the city, and gather the poor and the disabled, the lame and the blind, and bring them here.’
And the servant said, ‘Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
And the master said to the servant, ‘Go out to the roads and hedges, and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled.
For I tell you that not one of those men who were invited will taste my supper. For many are called, but few are chosen.’”
The Lord told this parable: “A man had two sons.
And the younger of the two sons said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.’ And he divided his property between them.
And not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and left for a distant country. While there, he squandered his property in reckless living.
And when he had spent everything, a severe famine arose in that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and hired himself out to one of the inhabitants of that country, who sent him into his fields to tend pigs.
He longed to fill himself with the pods the pigs were eating, but no one gave him anything.
Thinking it over, he said to himself, “How many of my father’s hired workers have more than enough bread, while I am dying of hunger here!
I will get up and go to my father and say to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Treat me as one of your hired workers.’”
He got up and went to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and felt compassion for him. He ran, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
The son said to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am not worthy to be called your son. Treat me as one of your hired workers.”
But the father said to his servants, “Quickly bring out the best robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and slaughter it, and let us eat and celebrate.
For this son was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.” And they began to celebrate.
His older son was in the field. As he came near the house, he heard singing and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked what this meant.
The servant said to him, “Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf because he has received him back safe and sound.”
He became angry and would not go in. His father came out and pleaded with him.
But he answered his father, “Look, I have served you all these years and have never disobeyed your command, yet you have never given me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son came, who had consumed your property with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.”
He said to him, “My child, you are always with me, and everything I have is yours.
But it was right to celebrate and rejoice, because this brother of yours was dead and has come back to life; he was lost and has been found.”
The Lord said, “Whoever is faithful in very little is also faithful in much, and whoever is dishonest in very little is also faithful in much.
So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will trust you with true wealth?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what is your own?
No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate one and love the other, or he will hold to one and begin to neglect the other. You cannot serve God and Mammon.”
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all these things and mocked him.
He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For what is highly valued among people is detestable before God.”
The Lord told this parable: “There was a rich man who dressed in purple and fine linen and lived in splendid enjoyment every day.
There was a poor man named Lazarus, who lay covered with sores at his gate.
The poor man died and was carried by angels to Abraham’s embrace. The rich man also died, and they buried him.
In Hades, being in torment, he lifted his eyes and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus in his embrace.
He called out and said, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame.”
Abraham said, “Child, remember that you received good things during your life, and Lazarus likewise received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are suffering.
And besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor can those from there cross over to us.”
He said, “Then I beg you, father, to send Lazarus to my father’s house,
for I have five brothers, so that he may warn them, lest they too come to this place of torment.”
Abraham said, “They have Moses and the prophets; let them listen to them.”
But he said, “No, Father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.”
He said to him, “If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not believe even if someone rises from the dead.”
The Lord said, “Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive
him. And if he sins against you seven times in a day and returns to you seven times, saying, ‘I repent,’ forgive him.”
The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
The Lord said, “If you had faith like a mustard seed, you would say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and stand in the sea,’ and it would obey you.
Which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, ‘Come at once and sit down to eat’?
Will he not instead say, ‘Prepare something for supper, fasten your belt, and serve me while I eat and drink; afterward you may eat and drink’?
Does he thank that servant because he did what was commanded? I do not think
so. So you too, when you have done what you were commanded, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done what we were obliged to do.’”
At that time, as Jesus was entering a certain village, ten men with leprosy met him. They stood at a distance
and raised their voices, saying, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.”
When Jesus saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” And as they went, they were all cleansed.
One of them, seeing that he was healed, returned, glorifying God aloud.
He came to Jesus, fell face down at his feet, and gave him thanks. He was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered and said to him, “Were not ten cleansed? But the nine
Was no one found who returned to give glory to God except this one foreigner?
And he said to him, “Go; your faith will save you.”
The Lord told this parable: “There was a judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor respected people.
There was a widow in that city who kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
For a long time he refused, but afterward he said to himself, ‘Although I neither fear God nor respect people,
because this widow keeps troubling me, I will give her justice, so that she will not wear me out by continually coming.’”
And the Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge says.
Will not God bring justice for his chosen ones, who cry out to him day and night? Will he delay over them?
I tell you that he will bring them justice quickly.”
The Lord told this parable:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself, saying, ‘God, I give you thanks that I am not like other people—robbers, wrongdoers, adulterers—or like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week and give a tenth of everything I acquire.’ But
the tax collector, standing far off, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner.’
I tell you, this man will go home justified rather than the other, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
At that time, a man came to Jesus, testing him and saying, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not murder. Do not commit adultery. Do not steal. Do not bear false witness. Honor your father and mother.”
He said to him, “I have kept all these from my youth.”
When Jesus heard this, he said to him, “There is still one thing you have not done. Sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come, follow me.”
When he heard this, he became deeply distressed, for he was very rich.
Seeing that he was deeply distressed, Jesus said, “It is hard for someone who has wealth to enter the kingdom of God.
For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Those who heard this said, “Who can be saved?”
He said, “What is impossible for people is possible for God.”

They led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning, and they did not enter the headquarters themselves, so that they would not become defiled but could eat the Passover.
Pilate went outside to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
They answered him, “If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you.”
Pilate said, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Jews said to him, “We are not permitted to put anyone to death.”
This was to fulfill the words Jesus had spoken, indicating what kind of death he was going to die.
Pilate went back into the governor’s headquarters and spoke to Jesus, saying to him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
Jesus answered him, “Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about me?”
Pilate answered him, “Am I a Jew? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”

Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my servants would have fought to keep me from being handed over to the Jews. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

Pilate said to him, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that [?] is a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”
Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went outside again to the Jews and told them, “I find no charge against him.”
“You have a custom that I release someone to you at Passover. Do you want me to release the king of the Jews to you?”
They all shouted, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
The Lord said to his disciples, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces and the places of honor at dinners.”
“They devour widows’ houses and make long prayers as a pretense. They will receive greater condemnation.”
Looking up, he saw rich people putting their gifts into the treasury.
He also saw a poor widow putting two coins [?] into it.
He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all the others.”
“For all these people contributed gifts to God out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had.”
The Lord said, “Be careful not to be deceived. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time is near.’ Do not follow them.”
“When you hear of wars and unrest, do not be afraid. These things must happen first, but the end will not come yet.”
“For they will lay their hands on you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons, and you will be brought before kings and rulers because of my name.”
“This will become an opportunity for you to testify. So settle it in your hearts not to prepare your defense beforehand.”
“For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or answer.”
“They will be betrayed by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.”
And you will be hated by everyone because of my name.
And not a hair of your head will perish.
By your endurance, gain your souls.
And there will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, and on earth distress among the nations, bewildered by the roaring and churning of the sea.
People will faint from fear and anticipation of what is coming upon the world, for the powers of heaven will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds with power and great glory.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Watch yourselves, lest your hearts become weighed down with overeating, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day come upon you suddenly.
For it will come like a trap upon everyone living on the face of the whole earth.
Therefore stay awake at all times, praying that you may be considered worthy to escape all these things that are going to happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
And an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
And being in agony, he prayed earnestly, and his sweat became like drops of blood falling to the ground.
Two other criminals were being led with Jesus to be put to death.
And when they came to the place called the Skull, there they crucified him and the criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
And Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.” And they divided his clothes, casting lots.
And the people stood watching. The rulers also mocked him along with them, saying, “He has saved others; let him save himself, if he is the Son of God, the Chosen One.”
And the soldiers also mocked him, coming up and offering him vinegar,
and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself.”
And there was also an inscription written above him in Greek, Latin, and Greek letters: “This is the King of the Jews.”
And one of the criminals who were hanging there insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us.”
But the other answered and rebuked him, saying, “Do you not fear God, since you are under the same condemnation?
But we two are condemned justly.
